newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai sugar sluggish, China news taken in stride.
newsitem.headline: Thai sugar sluggish, China news taken in stride.

text.p: The situation in Thai sugar market is anything but sweet, according trade and industry sources on Thursday.

Most mills were flush with stocks of raw sugar which have commanded very sluggish prices, but at the same time they were running out of white sugar for which demand is relatively strong, they told Reuters.

The industry took the news on Wednesday that China issued 500,000 tonnes of tolling licences in its stride as it did not expect the country to import substantial amounts until the white-to-raw premiums improved.
"The white-to-raw premiums now stands at around $60 per tonne or slightly higher...This is not the attractive level for tolling," said one trader from a US trading house.
"We do not expect any excitement in the raw market until the tolling is more profitable and China buys more," he said.

China recently bought 15,000 tonnes of raw sugar from Thailand for tolling. The suppliers included Mitsubishi and Cargill. One vessel was loading the sugar at a Thai port while the other arrived on Thursday.
Traders said they expected the raw premiums to move in a narrow range and around this current level for the whole season unless there were developments in other major producing countries.

"It would require natural disaster of a grand scale in major producing countries to move Thai raw premiums up substantially and I doubt if that will happen," said another trader. "Any improvement in demand from China will also help," he added.
They said most mills have committed 100 percent of their product. However, while stocks of raw sugar remained ample, all the white sugar was sold.
"There is almost no white sugar left for sale. Indonesia snapped up a big amount since the crushing started," said a miller.
However, Czarnikow forecast in a report earlier today that the Thai white sugar exports for 1996/97 season will be 1.2 million tonnes, which is below up to 1.35 million tonnes earlier forecast.
But it expected the raw sugar exports to reach 2.8 million tonnes despite the slow rate of shipments to date.

Thai raw sugar premiums for May/July deliveries were quoted at 0.22/0.30 US cents per lb over New York's Coffee Sugar and Cocoa Exchange (CSCE) futures on an FOB basis. July/September were quoted around 0.50/0.60 cents.
The production of Thai sugar has slowed down as 12 out of 46 mills closed operations for the season because of lower than expected sugar cane supplies.

Some millers said they did not expect the output this year to reach the 6.28-million-tonne target (tel quel) set by the government as the amount of sugar cane available was unlikely to exceed 60 million tonnes seen earlier and the yield was lower than that of last year.
"I still believe, and many have shared my view, that the maximum sugar cane this year was around 58 million tonnes," said an executive of a major sugar company.
Industry sources said some mills which based their sales on the projection set by the government had oversold and had to repurchase contracts.
As of April 10, the sugar output reached 5.71 million tonnes compared with 5.75 million during the corresponding period last year.
